name: wordfreq
algorithm: Count the word frequencies of a 50 MB text with each language's standard hash map, keys borrowed from the text, the map growing from empty; rounds times with a fresh map (README.md).

skip.c: no std hash map in C
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; counting has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own map; the checksum (FNV-1a of every distinct word times its count) checks that every map counted the same words
notes: Hashes and DoS posture (B20): mk Map.New, DD-5's fast fixed hash, public key; mk-keyed Map.NewKeyed, SipHash-1-3 under a random per-process key; Rust HashMap, SipHash-1-3 under RandomState's random key; Zig StringHashMap, Wyhash with seed 0, fixed; Go map, AES-based runtime hash seeded per map; C# Dictionary<string, ulong> with StringComparer.Ordinal and AlternateLookup<ReadOnlySpan<char>>, Marvin32 under a random per-process seed.
